taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Silphium albiflorum A.Gray as a Texas-native species.

evidence: Travis — University of Texas Plant Resources Center Travis County specimen/index evidence.
Burnet — documented occurrence at Doeskin Ranch, Balcones Canyonlands National Wildlife Refuge, Burnet County.
Mason — Texas Parks and Wildlife Department vascular flora of Mason Mountain Wildlife Management Area explicitly lists Silphium albiflorum.
BONAP/NAPA county mapping used as the project-wide county-distribution cross-check.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not infer Hays-local native status. The Purola/Hays source is explicitly introduced and is excluded from the native-county threshold.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with flower color and leaf shape. White rosinweed is the standout Silphium here because the ray florets are white, while the nearby project Silphium comparisons have yellow heads. Then confirm the tough rough/scabrous, often deeply divided foliage and dry calcareous-prairie habit.
best_field_traits: herbaceous perennial, often under about 1 m
leaves often deeply pinnately lobed or divided
dry limestone/calcareous prairie, open slopes and roadsides
morphology.key_separation: White rays are the fastest split from the yellow-headed project Silphium species. S. laciniatum may share deeply divided leaves but has yellow heads; S. radula has broad rough sessile leaves and yellow heads; S. integrifolium has broad entire leaves and yellow heads.
